title: Let’s rescue our friends
status: Narrative and blocking scaffold — not finished art
principle: Friends enjoy playing; bullies interrupt and capture them; Abbie and her dog set out to rescue them. No additional mythology.

scenes.title: An afternoon together
scenes.action: Fox lines up a shot. Bramble leans in, then looks at Fox with a friendly challenge.
visuals: Wide view of one clearing beneath the flowering tree; establishes the place we will return to.
Fox at left and Bramble at right, full bodies and readable faces; establishes the existing friends.
A small scratched play circle and a few ordinary-sized marbles between them; explains their activity without becoming the subject.
A few petals falling from the visible flowering canopy; connects motion to the setting.
Soft afternoon light and a dark teal root framing the pair; keeps faces readable.
scenes.sound: Leaf rustle, small movement sounds, a light playful musical phrase.
scenes.motion: Slow lateral drift of no more than 2%; sparse petals. No zoom into a marble.
scenes.transition: A reaction panel opens from the side toward which Fox looks.
needs: New wide action plate with BOTH approved character designs, relaxed posture, matching eyelines and full paws.
scenes.verdict: Composition and palette reference only. Existing image reads as concentration; it lacks clear shared enjoyment and Bramble’s clover details.

scenes.title: A little friendly teasing
scenes.understand: They are having fun with each other, not merely staring at objects.
scenes.action: Fox takes a shot and misses. Fox makes a sheepish face. Bramble laughs kindly; Fox joins in.
visuals: The same clearing remains behind the action to preserve location.
Medium shot of Fox making the shot; the paw belongs visibly to Fox, with the face still readable.
One narrow insert of the missed shot, less than a second, only if needed to explain the reaction.
Bramble’s laughing reaction panel followed by Fox’s sheepish smile; supplies cause and effect.
Consistent marbles, tree roots, screen positions and light; no unexplained scene change.
scenes.sound: One quiet marble click, a short shared laugh; music continues.
scenes.motion: Two panels enter in sequence, following shot → miss → reaction. Hold the expressions long enough to read.
scenes.transition: The laughter cuts off when Bramble looks beyond Fox.
needs: Fox shot pose and sheepish reaction.
Bramble laughing reaction with matching gaze and recognizable clover ornaments.
scenes.verdict: Current paw insert is too dominant and does not show a miss. Do not use it as proof of this action.

scenes.title: Someone blocks the light
scenes.action: Bramble stops laughing and looks up. Fox follows that gaze.
visuals: Same medium two-shot with both friends; their changed expressions are the subject.
A directional shadow crosses the play circle from the entrance side; it is cast by the approaching bullies.
Petals continue moving normally; the world does not magically freeze.
A restrained close-up of Bramble looking up; establishes the next cut’s eyeline.
scenes.sound: Music pauses; footsteps enter from the shadow side.
scenes.motion: Shadow crosses once. Camera settles. No blackout, screen shake, or ominous particle change.
scenes.transition: Eyeline cut to the approaching bullies.
needs: Shadow layer matching the bully silhouettes and scene lighting.
scenes.verdict: Missing. Smiling or concentrated portraits cannot substitute for surprised reactions.

scenes.title: The bullies spoil the game
scenes.understand: These bullies deliberately interrupt the friends’ fun.
scenes.action: Raze steps between the friends and scuffs the play circle. Vix blocks the way out. The friends draw together.
visuals: Raze enters from the established shadow side in the same clearing.
Raze’s foot disturbs the ring and moves a few marbles a short distance; shows the interruption without a hero-marble shot.
Vix is visible behind, blocking the path; makes the group threat legible.
Fox and Bramble together on the opposite side; preserves geography and their friendship.
One angled panel edge breaks the previously calm layout as Raze intrudes; visual emphasis belongs to his action.
scenes.text: Optional short line from Raze: “Game’s over.” No name card or narrator.
scenes.sound: Footstep, scuff, one short low musical accent.
scenes.motion: Raze crosses the panel boundary once; avoid repeated shakes or flashing.
scenes.transition: Cut on Vix moving toward the friends; do not skip the capture action.
scenes.verdict: Existing Raze portrait is an identity reference only. Folded arms do not communicate the scuff or capture.

scenes.title: The friends are taken
scenes.understand: The friends have been captured and are being taken up the path.
scenes.emotion: Unfairness, concern; clearly safe to rescue
scenes.action: Vix drops a loose rope net around both friends. Raze and Vix lead them up the path. Bramble looks back.
visuals: Panel one: net visibly descends around the friends; establishes how capture happens.
Panel two: both friends visible and unharmed inside roomy mesh, faces unobstructed; avoid constriction, pain or violent struggle.
Panel three: the same bullies and captured friends move uphill, in the same screen direction.
The play area is left behind in the lower foreground; links the loss to the fun we just saw.
scenes.text: Bramble calls “Abbie!” once. No explanatory caption.
scenes.sound: Soft rope movement, footsteps, the call; restrained music.
scenes.motion: Three deliberate cuts: capture → readable result → departure. No impact flash or comic violence.
scenes.transition: The call bridges to Abbie’s arrival at the clearing.
needs: Three matching action plates with net continuity and all four established characters.
Net is a proposed staging prop, not a new magical power or piece of lore.
scenes.verdict: Missing. Do not imply capture using smiling portraits, generic silhouettes, or a cut straight to empty ground.

scenes.title: Abbie sees what happened
scenes.understand: Abbie knows her friends need help and where they were taken.
scenes.action: Abbie and her dog enter the clearing as the call reaches them. She sees her friends being led away, then turns toward the path.
visuals: Abbie and her established unicorn Shih Tzu enter as a pair; exact approved designs required.
Disturbed play circle sits small in the foreground; continuity clue, not a mystery to solve.
Over Abbie’s shoulder, the friends and bullies remain visible on the near uphill path; provides direct evidence, not inferred tracking.
Close-up of Abbie’s face changing from concern to determination.
Dog looks along the same path beside her; establishes companionship without inventing powers.
scenes.sound: The distant call, a small concerned dog sound, a hopeful musical phrase begins.
scenes.motion: Cut along Abbie’s eyeline, then return to her resolved expression.
scenes.transition: Follow Abbie and the dog turning toward the mountain.
needs: Abbie/dog arrival two-shot and Abbie concerned/resolved expressions.
Verify an approved companion reference before generating; do not improvise its design.
scenes.verdict: Missing. Happy Abbie portrait is not an adequate concerned reaction; companion reference still needs verification.

scenes.title: There’s the way up
scenes.understand: The rescue route goes up this mountain.
scenes.action: Abbie and her dog face the path. The camera follows it upward, then settles back at the first playable stretch.
visuals: Abbie and dog small at the foot of the climb; provides scale and a clear starting point.
A continuous winding route climbs through the established mountain environment.
Cloud layers obscure portions of the higher route naturally; communicates distance without inventing a floating kingdom.
Return or dissolve to the matching first gameplay location; the mountain view must agree with the actual world.
scenes.text: Abbie: “Come on. Let’s get our friends.”
scenes.sound: Hopeful phrase rises; wind replaces clearing ambience.
scenes.motion: One controlled upward pan, about four seconds. Reduced motion uses three stationary views.
scenes.transition: Match the path position and horizon to the game camera.
needs: Reviewed tall climb plate with legible continuous route.
Matching foreground Abbie/dog layers and first gameplay frame.
scenes.verdict: Existing tall climb art must be inspected for route and color continuity before use; not cleared by filename alone.

scenes.title: The player takes over
scenes.understand: I am helping Abbie rescue her friends.
scenes.action: The camera rests at the start. Abbie is ready. The player taps to begin.
visuals: The real first gameplay view, sharing the preceding path alignment.
Abbie and dog in their starting positions if supported by the actual game scene.
One large accessible button: “Let’s rescue them.”
Normal game controls appear only after the tap; no fake gameplay or unexplained collectibles.
scenes.sound: Music continues across the handoff without restarting.
scenes.motion: Letterbox edges withdraw gently; input transfers exactly once. Reduced motion cuts directly.
scenes.transition: Emit the standalone completion event; production host owns starting gameplay.
needs: Verified first gameplay view and host completion callback.
scenes.verdict: Scaffold can emit a completion event, but production game integration remains absent.
